entries.title: 'npm is not recognized' / 'node: command not found'
entries.summary: Node.js is not installed, or this terminal started before PATH was updated.
entries.when: Right after installing Node, or in a new terminal type.

code: 1. Close ALL terminals (and VS Code) and reopen.
2. Still missing: install via the Node menu (NVM on Linux/WSL, nvm-windows or winget on Windows).
3. WSL: Windows' Node is not WSL's Node. Install Node inside WSL too.
steps.label: Fix

troubleshooting: With NVM: run 'nvm use --lts' (Linux) or 'nvm use lts' (Windows) in the new terminal.

entries.title: PowerShell: 'running scripts is disabled on this system'
entries.summary: PowerShell blocks the npm.ps1 wrapper script.
entries.when: npm/npx fail in Windows PowerShell with an UnauthorizedAccess message.

steps.label: Alternative without changing policy: call npm.cmd
steps.dir: Project root (the folder that contains package.json)

entries.warning: This changes a Windows security setting for your user account. Only do it on your own machine.
troubleshooting: This only changes policy for your user, allowing local scripts and signed remote scripts.

entries.title: npm ERESOLVE: unable to resolve dependency tree
entries.summary: Two packages require incompatible versions of a shared dependency (often React).
entries.where: Project root (the folder that contains package.json)

steps.label: 1. See which React version is installed
steps.dir: Project root (the folder that contains package.json)

steps.label: 2. LAST RESORT: ignore peer conflicts
steps.dir: Project root (the folder that contains package.json)

code: Better: upgrade/downgrade the package named in the error to a version that supports your React version.
steps.label: Preferred fix

entries.warning: --legacy-peer-deps can hide real incompatibilities; test the app after using it.
entries.expected: npm completes and the app runs.
troubleshooting: Use the same flag consistently for the project and note it in the README.
Do not combine --force with random package edits.

entries.title: 'Cannot find module' / 'Failed to resolve import'
entries.summary: The import path is wrong, the file name case differs, or the package is not installed.
entries.when: Red error overlay or terminal error after adding an import.
entries.where: Project root (the folder that contains package.json)

code: - Case matters on Linux/Netlify: Card.jsx != card.jsx.
- Run: npm install axios (name must match package.json).
steps.label: Check
List exact file names
steps.dir: Project root (the folder that contains package.json)

entries.expected: The import resolves and the error overlay disappears.
troubleshooting: After renaming a file on Windows/macOS, Git may not notice a case-only change: git mv Old.jsx New.jsx.

entries.title: 'Invalid hook call' / hooks rules errors
keywords: hooks can only be called inside
entries.summary: Hooks used outside a component, inside conditions, or two React copies installed.
entries.where: Project root (the folder that contains package.json)

code: - Call useState/useEffect only at the TOP of a function component (never in if/loops/handlers).
- Component names start with a capital letter.
steps.label: Code checks
Duplicate versions of React?
steps.dir: Project root (the folder that contains package.json)

entries.expected: One version of react and react-dom, no hook error.
troubleshooting: Duplicates: remove node_modules and reinstall (Clean reinstall).

entries.title: Blank white page / nothing renders
entries.summary: A runtime error stopped rendering, or the router/root is misconfigured.
entries.when: Dev or deployed site shows an empty page.

code: 1. Browser DevTools (F12) > Console: read the first red error.
2. Terminal running 'npm run dev': any error?
3. index.html still has <div id="root"> and the main.jsx script?
6. Deployed only? Check 'base' in vite.config and SPA redirects (Running > Netlify).
steps.label: Checklist

entries.expected: You find the first real error.
troubleshooting: Fix the FIRST error; later ones are often side effects.

entries.title: import.meta.env.VITE_X is undefined
entries.summary: The variable name, file name, or restart is wrong.
entries.when: Config values are undefined in the browser.

entries.title: CORS error when calling an API
entries.summary: The browser blocks requests to another origin unless the server allows it.
entries.when: fetch to your backend fails in the browser but works in Postman/curl.

steps.label: Dev: proxy /api to the backend, then fetch('/api/...') (restart Vite)

entries.expected: Requests to /api reach the backend without CORS errors.
troubleshooting: Production: configure CORS headers on the backend (e.g. Flask-CORS / FastAPI CORSMiddleware) for your site's origin.

entries.title: 404 when refreshing /about on a deployed site
entries.summary: The server looks for an /about file; a single-page app only has index.html.
entries.when: Links work, but refresh or direct URL gives 404 online.
entries.where: Project root (the folder that contains package.json)

steps.label: Netlify: add this file, rebuild and redeploy

entries.expected: Direct visits to /about load the app.
troubleshooting: Other hosts need an equivalent 'rewrite all to index.html' rule.

entries.title: EACCES permission denied on npm install -g
entries.summary: npm tries to write to a system folder.

code: Do NOT use sudo npm. Use NVM (Node menu) so global packages go in your home folder.
Most tools do not need -g: use npx or project-local installs.
steps.label: Fix

troubleshooting: Wrong owner on node_modules from an earlier sudo? Delete node_modules and reinstall as your normal user.
